title: Numbers Chapter 11 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Numbers chapter 11 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Numbers Chapter 11 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Numbers Chapter 11.

questions.question: What did the LORD do when the people complained in the camp?
options: His anger was kindled and fire burnt among them
He gave them meat to eat
questions.correctAnswer: His anger was kindled and fire burnt among them
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:1 states that the LORD's anger was kindled and the fire of the LORD burnt among them when the people complained.

questions.question: What happened when the people cried unto Moses and he prayed to the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: The fire was quenched
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:2 tells us that when Moses prayed to the LORD after the people cried to him, the fire was quenched.

questions.question: What name was given to the place where the fire of the LORD burnt among the people?
questions.correctAnswer: Taberah
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:3 says the place was named Taberah because the fire of the LORD burnt among them.

questions.question: Who among the people fell a lusting and caused the children of Israel to weep for flesh to eat?
questions.correctAnswer: The mixed multitude
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:4 specifies that the mixed multitude among them fell a lusting and made the children of Israel weep for flesh.

questions.question: Which of these foods did the Israelites remember eating freely in Egypt?
options: Fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic
questions.correctAnswer: Fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:5 lists these foods as those the Israelites remembered eating in Egypt.

questions.question: How did the people describe their soul because of eating only manna?
questions.correctAnswer: Dried away
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:6 says their soul was dried away because there was nothing besides manna before their eyes.

questions.question: What was manna compared to in size and color?
options: Coriander seed and the color of bdellium
questions.correctAnswer: Coriander seed and the color of bdellium
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:7 describes manna as like coriander seed and colored like bdellium.

questions.question: How did the people prepare the manna after gathering it?
options: They ground it in mills, beat it in mortars, baked it in pans, and made cakes
They ate it raw as it fell
questions.correctAnswer: They ground it in mills, beat it in mortars, baked it in pans, and made cakes
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:8 explains that the people ground manna in mills or beat it in mortars and baked it in pans to make cakes.

questions.question: When did manna fall upon the camp?
options: During the day when the sun was hot
When the dew fell upon the camp in the night
questions.correctAnswer: When the dew fell upon the camp in the night
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:9 states manna fell upon the camp when the dew fell in the night.

questions.question: What was Moses' reaction when he heard the people weeping throughout their families?
options: He was displeased and the LORD's anger was kindled greatly
questions.correctAnswer: He was displeased and the LORD's anger was kindled greatly
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:10 says Moses was displeased and the LORD's anger was greatly kindled when he heard the people weeping.

questions.question: True or False: Moses asked the LORD why he had found favor in His sight to carry the burden of all the people.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:11 shows Moses asking why he had NOT found favor in the LORD's sight to bear the people's burden, not that he had found favor.

questions.question: True or False: Moses expressed that he was able to bear the burden of all the people alone.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:14 clearly states Moses was not able to bear all the people alone because it was too heavy for him.

questions.question: True or False: Moses asked the LORD to kill him if he had found favor in His sight.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:15 records Moses asking the LORD to kill him if he had found favor, so he would not see his wretchedness.

questions.question: True or False: Moses was instructed to gather seventy elders of Israel to help bear the burden of the people.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:16 states the LORD told Moses to gather seventy elders to help bear the burden of the people.

questions.question: In Numbers 11, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Gather seventy elders to help Moses
Moses prays to quench the fire
Tell the people to sanctify themselves to eat flesh
The LORD sends quails to the camp
questions.correctAnswer: Moses prays to quench the fire
questions.explanation: According to Numbers 11:2, Moses prayed to the LORD and the fire was quenched before the other instructions and events happened.

medium.title: Numbers Chapter 11 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Numbers Chapter 11 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What burden does Moses express in his prayer to the LORD in Numbers 11:13-15?
options: He feels unable to provide flesh for the people and overwhelmed by their demands
He is worried about the lack of water in the wilderness
He complains about the people's disobedience to the law
He asks for more leaders to help conquer the land
questions.correctAnswer: He feels unable to provide flesh for the people and overwhelmed by their demands
questions.explanation: In Numbers 11:13-15, Moses expresses frustration at being unable to give flesh to the people who weep to him for it and says he cannot bear the burden alone, even asking God to kill him if this continues.

questions.question: According to Numbers 11:16, who does the LORD instruct Moses to gather to help bear the burden of the people?
options: Seventy elders of Israel who are known to be leaders and officers
questions.correctAnswer: Seventy elders of Israel who are known to be leaders and officers
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:16 instructs Moses to gather seventy elders who are leaders and officers to stand with him at the tabernacle to help bear the people's burden.

questions.question: What does the LORD promise to do with the spirit upon Moses in Numbers 11:17?
options: Take some of the spirit upon Moses and put it upon the seventy elders to help bear the burden
Remove the spirit from Moses and give it all to the elders
Increase the spirit's power only on Moses
Send an angel to lead the elders
questions.correctAnswer: Take some of the spirit upon Moses and put it upon the seventy elders to help bear the burden
questions.explanation: In Numbers 11:17, the LORD promises to take some of the spirit upon Moses and give it to the seventy elders so they may share the responsibility.

questions.question: What instruction does Moses give the people in Numbers 11:18 regarding eating flesh?
options: Sanctify yourselves against tomorrow to eat flesh because the LORD will provide it
Continue eating manna only and avoid flesh
Gather fruits and vegetables instead of flesh
Prepare to fast for a week before eating flesh
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctify yourselves against tomorrow to eat flesh because the LORD will provide it
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:18 instructs Moses to tell the people to sanctify themselves by the next day because the LORD will give them flesh to eat as they requested.

questions.question: How long does the LORD say the people will eat flesh according to Numbers 11:19-20?
options: For a whole month until it becomes loathsome to them
Only one day as a special feast
Three days to satisfy their craving
Until they reach the promised land
questions.correctAnswer: For a whole month until it becomes loathsome to them
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:19-20 explains the people will eat flesh not just for a few days but for a whole month until it comes out of their nostrils and they grow disgusted, because they despised the LORD and complained about leaving Egypt.

questions.question: What concern does Moses raise in Numbers 11:21-22 about providing flesh for the people?
options: Whether the flocks, herds, and fish are sufficient to feed six hundred thousand men for a month
That the people will reject flesh and prefer manna
That the elders will refuse to help gather the meat
That the journey will be delayed due to hunting
questions.correctAnswer: Whether the flocks, herds, and fish are sufficient to feed six hundred thousand men for a month
questions.explanation: In Numbers 11:21-22, Moses questions how there will be enough animals or fish to provide flesh for all six hundred thousand men for an entire month.

questions.question: What does the LORD ask Moses in Numbers 11:23 to demonstrate His power?
options: If His hand is waxed short, implying whether His word will fail or not
If Moses will obey His commands without question
If the elders are worthy to share the spirit
If the people will repent of their complaints
questions.correctAnswer: If His hand is waxed short, implying whether His word will fail or not
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:23 has the LORD asking Moses if His power (hand) is shortened, indicating that Moses will see if God's word comes to pass or not, demonstrating His capability.

questions.question: What action does Moses take in Numbers 11:24 after receiving the LORD's command about the elders?
options: He tells the people the LORD's words and gathers seventy elders around the tabernacle
He prays alone without telling anyone
He sends spies to find food
He orders a fast for the people
questions.correctAnswer: He tells the people the LORD's words and gathers seventy elders around the tabernacle
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:24 states Moses went out, told the people the LORD's words, and gathered the seventy elders to set them around the tabernacle as instructed.

questions.question: How does Numbers 11:25 describe the Spirit coming upon the seventy elders?
options: The LORD came down in a cloud, spoke to Moses, and gave the spirit to the elders who prophesied
The elders received the spirit silently without speaking
The elders were frightened and ran away
The spirit left Moses completely and only rested on the elders
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD came down in a cloud, spoke to Moses, and gave the spirit to the elders who prophesied
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:25 describes the LORD descending in a cloud, speaking to Moses, taking some of the spirit upon him and giving it to the seventy elders, who then prophesied without ceasing.

questions.question: What is significant about Eldad and Medad as mentioned in Numbers 11:26?
options: They prophesied in the camp though they were not with the seventy elders at the tabernacle
They refused to receive the spirit
They were chosen as leaders of the tribes
questions.correctAnswer: They prophesied in the camp though they were not with the seventy elders at the tabernacle
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:26 notes that Eldad and Medad, though written among the elders, did not go to the tabernacle but yet the spirit rested on them and they prophesied in the camp.

questions.question: What is Joshua's reaction to Eldad and Medad prophesying in Numbers 11:28?
options: He asks Moses to forbid them from prophesying
He encourages them to prophesy more
He reports them to the priests for punishment
questions.correctAnswer: He asks Moses to forbid them from prophesying
questions.explanation: In Numbers 11:28, Joshua, Moses' servant, tells Moses to forbid Eldad and Medad from prophesying, showing concern over their actions.

questions.question: How does Moses respond to Joshua's request in Numbers 11:29?
options: He wishes that all the LORD's people were prophets and that the LORD would put His spirit upon them
He agrees to forbid Eldad and Medad
He prays for Eldad and Medad
questions.correctAnswer: He wishes that all the LORD's people were prophets and that the LORD would put His spirit upon them
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:29 shows Moses responding positively, wishing all the LORD's people were prophets and that His spirit would be upon them, not restricting prophecy.

questions.question: True or False: According to Numbers 11:14, Moses says he can bear the burden of all the people alone.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: In Numbers 11:14, Moses explicitly states he is not able to bear all the people alone because the burden is too heavy for him.

questions.question: True or False: Numbers 11:20 teaches that the people will grow to loathe eating flesh because they despised the LORD among them and complained about leaving Egypt.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:20 explains the flesh will become loathsome to them after a whole month of eating it because they despised the LORD and wept, regretting leaving Egypt.

questions.question: True or False: According to Numbers 11:23, the LORD's power is limited and He cannot fulfill His promise to provide flesh.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:23 shows the LORD rhetorically asking if His hand is waxed short, implying His power is not limited and His word will come to pass, demonstrating His capability to fulfill the promise.

hard.title: Numbers Chapter 11 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Numbers Chapter 11.

questions.question: What significant event occurred when the spirit rested upon the seventy elders of Israel?
options: They prophesied and did not cease
questions.correctAnswer: They prophesied and did not cease
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:25 states that when the spirit rested upon the seventy elders, they prophesied and did not cease, indicating the empowerment by God's Spirit for prophetic ministry.

questions.question: Who were Eldad and Medad, according to Numbers 11?
options: Priests who officiated at the tabernacle
Two men who prophesied in the camp but did not go to the tabernacle
questions.correctAnswer: Two men who prophesied in the camp but did not go to the tabernacle
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:26 explains that Eldad and Medad were two men who had the spirit rest upon them and they prophesied in the camp though they did not go out to the tabernacle.

questions.question: What was Joshua's reaction when he heard Eldad and Medad prophesying in the camp?
options: He asked Moses to forbid them
questions.correctAnswer: He asked Moses to forbid them
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:28 records that Joshua asked Moses to forbid Eldad and Medad from prophesying, showing his protective loyalty to Moses' leadership.

questions.question: How did Moses respond to Joshua's request to forbid Eldad and Medad from prophesying?
options: He expressed envy for their spiritual gifts
He wished all the Lord's people were prophets
questions.correctAnswer: He wished all the Lord's people were prophets
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:29 shows Moses saying he wished all the LORD's people were prophets and that God would put His spirit upon them, revealing Moses' desire for widespread spiritual empowerment.

questions.question: What natural phenomenon accompanied God's provision of quails to the Israelites?
options: A wind from the LORD bringing quails from the sea
questions.correctAnswer: A wind from the LORD bringing quails from the sea
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:31 describes a wind from the LORD that brought quails from the sea and let them fall around the camp, showing God's miraculous provision.

questions.question: For how long did the Israelites eat quail according to God's warning?
questions.correctAnswer: A whole month
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:20 says the Israelites would eat quail for a whole month until it came out at their nostrils and was loathsome, illustrating the consequences of their lust.

questions.question: What was Moses’ concern about providing flesh to the people?
options: He doubted God’s power to provide
He questioned where enough flesh could come from for six hundred thousand footmen
He feared the people would reject it
He wanted to preserve the flocks
questions.correctAnswer: He questioned where enough flesh could come from for six hundred thousand footmen
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:21-22 shows Moses doubting how so many people could be supplied with enough flesh from flocks, herds, or fish, expressing the logistical challenge.

questions.question: What was God's response to Moses' doubt about providing flesh to the people?
options: God told Moses to prepare the flocks
God assured Moses His hand was not shortened and His word would come to pass
God gave Moses a new plan
questions.correctAnswer: God assured Moses His hand was not shortened and His word would come to pass
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:23 records God's rhetorical question asking if His hand is waxed short and assuring Moses that his word will come to pass, affirming God's power.

questions.question: What was the name given to the place where the people who lusted were buried, and what does it mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Kibrothhattaavah, meaning 'graves of craving'
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:34 states the place was named Kibrothhattaavah because there they buried the people that lusted, linking the name to their craving and death.

questions.question: Where did the people journey after leaving Kibrothhattaavah?
questions.correctAnswer: Hazeroth
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:35 records that after Kibrothhattaavah, the people journeyed to Hazeroth and stayed there, continuing their wilderness journey.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently exemplified by the contrast between the people's complaints about manna and God's provision of quail?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: The narrative in Numbers 11 uses chiasm by framing the people's dissatisfaction with manna and God's response with quail provision, highlighting reversal and contrast in the story.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word 'Taberah,' and why was this place named so?
options: It means 'fire' because the fire of the LORD burnt among them
It means 'desert' because it was dry
It means 'camp' because they camped there
It means 'lament' because people wept there
questions.correctAnswer: It means 'fire' because the fire of the LORD burnt among them
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:3 explains that the place was named Taberah because the fire of the LORD burnt among the people there; 'Taberah' means 'burning' or 'fire'.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of the Spirit resting on multiple believers as seen in Numbers 11?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:17-18 quotes Joel's prophecy about God pouring out His Spirit on all people, echoing Numbers 11 where the Spirit is given to many elders, showing fulfillment of Spirit empowerment.

questions.question: How does the theme of God's provision and people's complaints in Numbers 11 connect with the wilderness testing of Israel in Deuteronomy 8:2-3?
options: Both emphasize the importance of manna as a permanent food source
Both highlight God's testing of Israel's faith through provision and hardship
Both describe the conquest of Canaan
Both focus on the laws given at Sinai
questions.correctAnswer: Both highlight God's testing of Israel's faith through provision and hardship
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 8:2-3 recounts how God led Israel in the wilderness to humble and test them by providing manna, paralleling Numbers 11 where provision and complaints reveal testing and faith challenges.

questions.question: True or False: Moses felt fully capable and not burdened by leading the Israelites as described in Numbers 11.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:14-15 reveal Moses expressing that he is not able to bear all the people alone because the burden is too heavy, showing his distress and burden in leadership.

theological.title: Numbers Chapter 11 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Numbers Chapter 11 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily demonstrated by God's reaction to the people's complaints in Numbers 11:1?
questions.correctAnswer: God's wrath
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:1 shows that the LORD's anger was kindled and fire burnt among the people as a direct response to their complaints, demonstrating God's attribute of wrath against sin.

questions.question: According to Numbers 11:4-6, what does the people's longing for flesh instead of manna reveal about human nature in the wilderness context?
options: Human susceptibility to craving and forgetfulness of past deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: Human susceptibility to craving and forgetfulness of past deliverance
questions.explanation: Verses 4-6 depict the people lusting after flesh and reminiscing about the food in Egypt, showing their forgetfulness of God's miraculous provision (manna) and revealing human craving for worldly comforts despite divine provision.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is reflected in Moses' lament about bearing the people's burden alone in Numbers 11:11-15?
options: Doctrine of the priesthood's mediatorial role
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of the priesthood's mediatorial role
questions.explanation: Moses' plea in verses 11-15 highlights the burdensome role of a mediator between God and people, reflecting the priestly or prophetic mediatorial function in bearing the people's burdens before God.

questions.question: How does God's instruction to Moses to gather seventy elders in Numbers 11:16-17 reveal an aspect of divine governance?
options: God's delegation of authority to human leaders
questions.correctAnswer: God's delegation of authority to human leaders
questions.explanation: In verses 16-17, God commands Moses to gather seventy elders so that the Spirit upon Moses is shared with them to help bear the people's burden, demonstrating God's governance through delegated human leadership.

questions.question: What does the promise of eating flesh 'until it come out at your nostrils' in Numbers 11:18-20 teach about God's justice and judgment?
options: God's use of judgment to correct ingratitude
questions.correctAnswer: God's use of judgment to correct ingratitude
questions.explanation: Verses 18-20 indicate that God will give the people meat to eat for a whole month until they loathe it, as a judgment for despising Him and complaining about deliverance, showing corrective justice.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exhibited in God's rhetorical question to Moses, 'Is the LORD'S hand waxed short?' in Numbers 11:23?
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipotence
questions.explanation: In verse 23, God challenges Moses' doubt by asking rhetorically if His hand is shortened, thereby emphasizing His unlimited power (omnipotence) to fulfill His word.

questions.question: What does the Spirit resting on the seventy elders and their prophesying in Numbers 11:25-26 indicate about the Spirit's role in communal leadership?
options: Spirit's exclusive presence on Moses only
Spirit's empowerment for shared prophetic ministry
questions.correctAnswer: Spirit's empowerment for shared prophetic ministry
questions.explanation: Verses 25-26 describe how the LORD took of the Spirit upon Moses and gave it to seventy elders, enabling them to prophesy, which reveals the Spirit's role in empowering communal leadership for prophecy and governance.

questions.question: In the narrative arc of redemption, what does the quail provision in Numbers 11:31-32 foreshadow about God's provision in Christ?
options: Christ as the bread of life providing spiritual nourishment
Christ as a warrior king delivering Israel physically
Christ as a strict judge punishing sin
Christ as a prophet predicting famine
questions.correctAnswer: Christ as the bread of life providing spiritual nourishment
questions.explanation: The provision of quail as physical sustenance in verses 31-32, alongside manna, prefigures Christ who is the true bread of life, offering spiritual nourishment beyond physical needs (cf. John 6:35).

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God's holiness and justice is taught by the plague that struck the people while still eating the quail in Numbers 11:33?
questions.correctAnswer: God's holy judgment against rebellion
questions.explanation: Verse 33 reveals that while the flesh was still in their mouths, the LORD's wrath was kindled and He struck the people with a great plague, showing that God's holiness demands judgment upon sin and rebellion.

questions.question: How does the naming of the place 'Kibrothhattaavah' in Numbers 11:34 function theologically in the narrative?
options: As a place of God's blessing
As a memorial of divine judgment for lusting
As a symbol of Israel's victory
questions.correctAnswer: As a memorial of divine judgment for lusting
questions.explanation: Verse 34 records that the place was named Kibrothhattaavah, meaning 'graves of lust,' marking the site where God judged those who lusted after flesh, serving as a theological reminder of consequences of sinful craving.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's giving of quails for a whole month would be impossible given the population size. What does Numbers 11:21-23 actually teach about God's power and promise?
options: God lacks power to provide for many
God's promises are conditional on human effort
God's power is unlimited and His word will be fulfilled
questions.correctAnswer: God's power is unlimited and His word will be fulfilled
questions.explanation: Verses 21-23 show Moses doubting the practical provision for 600,000 men, but God asserts His omnipotence, asking if His hand is shortened and affirming that His word will come to pass, highlighting divine sovereignty over nature and promise.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Numbers 11:4-6 and Numbers 11:10-15 provide about human sinfulness and leadership burdens?
options: Human sinfulness is minimal and leadership is easy
Human sinfulness causes complaint and leaders face heavy burdens
Complaints are unrelated to leadership challenges
questions.correctAnswer: Human sinfulness causes complaint and leaders face heavy burdens
questions.explanation: The people's complaints about food in verses 4-6 reveal human sinfulness and ingratitude, while Moses' lament in verses 10-15 shows the heavy burden leaders bear in managing sinful people, illustrating the interrelation of human sin and leadership challenges.

questions.question: What theological teaching about the Spirit’s distribution and prophetic ministry is found by synthesizing Numbers 11:17 and Numbers 11:25-26?
options: The Spirit is given only to Moses
The Spirit is shared among many to empower communal leadership and prophecy
The Spirit is withdrawn after Moses
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit is shared among many to empower communal leadership and prophecy
questions.explanation: Verse 17 promises the Spirit will be taken from Moses and given to seventy elders to share the leadership burden; verses 25-26 show this Spirit enabling the elders to prophesy, teaching divine empowerment for shared spiritual ministry.

questions.question: What does the combined narrative from Numbers 11:31-32 and Numbers 11:33-34 teach about the tension between God's provision and human disobedience?
options: God provides without regard to human response
God's provision can be met with judgment when met with disobedience
God's provision is only a test
questions.correctAnswer: God's provision can be met with judgment when met with disobedience
questions.explanation: Verses 31-32 show God providing abundant quail, yet verses 33-34 reveal that the people's disobedience and lust led to a deadly plague, teaching that divine provision does not excuse rebellion but coexists with holy judgment.

questions.question: What does Numbers 11:28-29 teach about Moses' attitude toward prophetic ministry and the Spirit's work among God's people?
options: Moses is jealous and forbids others from prophesying
Moses desires all God's people to be prophets and to receive the Spirit
Moses is indifferent to prophetic ministry
Moses limits prophecy to the seventy elders only
questions.correctAnswer: Moses desires all God's people to be prophets and to receive the Spirit
questions.explanation: In verses 28-29, Moses does not forbid Eldad and Medad from prophesying but rather expresses a wish that all God's people were prophets and that the Spirit would be upon them, showing an inclusive, Spirit-empowered vision.
